why: The parent reduced ordered chord error from 30/38 to 25/38 but produced zero parseable outputs and melody error of 1.0 because its melody dependency was unavailable. A bounded integration repair tests whether that measured chord gain can become usable without confounding it with new recognition rules. Three experiments remain; this isolates the immediate blocker before exploring another recognizer.
hypothesis: Missing melody artifacts and serialization failures, rather than the chord OCR stage itself, explain the parent's unusable output; restoring image-derived melody can retain its chord gain while recovering baseline melody performance.
expected_observation: Seven parseable melody-plus-harmony outputs with melody error at or below 87/130 and chord error at or below 25/38. Failure to recover melody or retain these scores would falsify the proposed integration benefit.
